name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details better than standard upscalers by using depth maps to guide the scaling, which directly improves output quality without extra compute overhead. The trade-off is extra setup time to integrate the ComfyUI node, but the quality gain outweighs the hassle.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscalers won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core problem is motion blur from low frame rates, not resolution. Flowframes’ VFI won’t fix it either—its motion interpolation is tuned for smoothness, not facial detail retention. The real risk is wasting time on tools that don’t address the bottleneck; test a frame-doubling VFI model like *FILM* or *RIFE* first—if face fidelity improves, then upscaling matters.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add Flowframes’ VFI module to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. Motion blur in source frames destroys facial detail, and Flowframes’ VFI sharpens motion between frames by estimating true motion paths—this directly attacks the root cause of EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop. The trade-off is a small runtime increase per frame, but the quality gain outweighs it; depth-aware upscalers won’t fix what motion blur breaks.

name: Torque
text: Flowframes’ VFI won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because it’s tuned for smooth motion, not facial detail retention—it’ll blur faces further by inventing motion where none exists. The real risk is wasting time on a tool that worsens the core problem. Test it on a 10-frame burst of a talking face: if facial features degrade after VFI, the argument is dead.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Skip both InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler and Flowframes’ VFI—test DiffBIR’s video mode for motion deblurring first, then apply Real-ESRGAN’s face model if needed. Torque owns the test; Gearbox owns the integration if DiffBIR works.
